title: The Man of Tango
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Angie, a tango teacher and exhibition dancer hailed as 'The Man of Tango', is drawn to Hiro, a half-Latin, half-Japanese man raised by his Japanese grandfather who does not see himself as interested in men (SuBLime blurb via AniList; MangaUpdates). Angie teaches Hiro the tango and a romance between adult men grows; a final chapter jumps about 30 years ahead (Comics Worth Reading review). One volume, published in English by SuBLime with a mature rating.
life_message: It presents passionate, embodied love found through dance as what makes a life feel fully lived (to verify).

content.note: MangaUpdates lists abuse, an abusive authority figure and a tragic past in backstory (to verify).
Grief over a family death (Comics Worth Reading); loneliness and difficult childhood (MangaUpdates).

Explicit sex scenes between adult men behind the mature rating (Comics Worth Reading; MangaUpdates Adult genre); nudity (AniList); an alcohol-fueled first encounter and dubious-consent label (MangaUpdates).
Alcohol-fueled encounter (Comics Worth Reading; MangaUpdates Drunken Intercourse).
Sex after drinking presented romantically (review; MangaUpdates).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: No honor conflicts noted; personal drama of grief and desire (review).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Hiro leaves his grandfather's custody-shaped life for dance (MangaUpdates).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Chosen partners and dance partners over family (review).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Teacher-student dance bond becomes partnership; reversible couple (MangaUpdates).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Personal choice over inherited identity (MangaUpdates Search for Oneself).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Passion and self-discovery through tango are the core (blurb; review).

folkways.japan: Hiro's identity as a mixed-heritage man raised as Japanese by his grandfather reflects Japanese expectations of conformity for those of mixed background (to verify).

delivery.evidence: Review describes a sensual romance with thin characterization, no message stated (Comics Worth Reading).
delivery.note: The story carries its view of love through the dance and the relationship rather than argument.

winners_losers: Angie and Hiro's love wins and lasts decades; Hiro's earlier 'not gay' self-image gives way, and the story's sympathy rests with passion and openness.
